newsitem.title: USA: FedEx aims 100 pct electronic transactions.
newsitem.headline: FedEx aims 100 pct electronic transactions.

text.p: Federal Express Corp has set its sights on weaning all customers from paper and voice transactions and moving them to the Internet and other electronic conduits like corporate intranets, Steve Braun, manager of electronic marketing commerce said.
"We want 100 percent of our customers doing 100 percent of their transactions online 100 percent of the time," Braun told the Journal of Commerce World Air Cargo Internet Symposium.
That will take years, but it is a goal set by top management.
Over 400,000 customers are online with FedEx today, and they generate over 60 percent of the company's over two million daily transactions, he said.
Braun is emphatic - the Internet is the first new medium since the advent of television, and it is destined to revolutionize communications and commerce.

Quoting FedEx Chief Executive Officer Fred Smith to an audience composed in large part of freight forwarders, cargo brokers and agents, Braun said the Internet would make it difficult for companies in any middleman function to stay in business unless they adapt to the changes being wrought by electronic commerce.
The growth rate of FedEx Internet transactions is 10-12 percent monthly, he said. In January, 800,000 packages were tracked via the Web.
"How many customer service reps would I have to add to process 800,000 tracks?" he said.
Braun said electronic bookings were cheaper to process but he declined to reveal by how much.

Many large FedEx customers have put links to FedEx's Internet track and trace system into their websites so that employees, even customers, can track a shipment without ever visiting FedEx on the web. Over half of all electronic tracking requests are initiated from customer websites, he said.
